open_points.subject: Registry validation for revoking project grants and assignments
open_points.text: “Portal mutation policy admits the grant and assignment operations of access management only on an answer whose `exists` and `is_active` are both true” conflicts with R0-24: “Revoking an existing viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant does not consult the Registry and succeeds for an archived project, also while the Registry is unavailable.”
open_points.question: Does the new `exists && is_active` condition apply only when creating a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant, or also when revoking one?
options: Apply it only to creation; revocation never consults Registry.
Apply it to both creation and revocation, superseding R0-24.
open_points.default_guess: Apply it only to creation and retain Registry-independent revocation.

witness.initial: An active viewer grant exists for a project that Registry has since archived.
events: An administrator requests revocation of the viewer grant.
outcomes: R0-24 permits the revocation without consulting Registry, so the grant becomes revoked.
The changed M17 sentence requires `exists && is_active`; the archived answer has `is_active = false`, so revocation is refused and the grant remains active.
witness.observer: The administrator and the viewer whose access was meant to be revoked.

open_points.subject: Consistency and authority of ProjectValidationResult lifecycle fields
open_points.text: “only on an answer whose `exists` and `is_active` are both true … and uses only `status` (`active` or not) in the project guard of State 2 A4/A5” while `ProjectValidationResult` independently contains `exists`, `status`, and `is_active` with no stated consistency invariant.
open_points.question: Which combinations of `exists`, `status`, and `is_active` are valid, is `is_active` derived from `exists` and `status`, and which rule controls when the fields disagree?
options: Require `is_active == (exists && status == active)` and reject inconsistent Registry answers.
Treat the fields independently: access-management creation requires `exists && is_active`, while the project guard independently trusts `status`.
Give one field or predicate explicit precedence over the others.
open_points.default_guess: Require `is_active == (exists && status == active)` and treat inconsistent answers as a Registry boundary failure.

witness.initial: The Registry gateway produces the model-valid result `exists=false`, `status="active"`, `is_active=true` for a requested project.
events: An administrator requests creation of a project assignment.
The access-management admission and the A5 project guard inspect the same result.
outcomes: The `exists && is_active` rule refuses creation because `exists` is false.
The status-only guard admits creation because `status` is active.
witness.observer: The administrator and the staff member whose assignment may or may not be created.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: Viewer project-list treatment of a Registry not-found result
set_aside.text: “a granted project, archived or not, whose Registry context cannot be obtained at that moment is left out of it rather than listed without context; once its context is obtained again it is listed again”
set_aside.question: Does “cannot be obtained at that moment” include a typed `not_found`/unknown-project answer, or only failures regarded as temporary dependency failures?
options: Omit the granted project for every failure to obtain ProjectContext, including `not_found`.
Omit it only for temporary Registry failures; handle a definitive `not_found` differently.
Fail the project-list read for definitive identity failures instead of silently omitting the grant.
set_aside.default_guess: Omit the project for any failure to obtain a valid ProjectContext, including `not_found`, while retaining the grant.

witness.initial: A viewer has an active grant for project P; Registry later answers `not_found` for P's context.
events: The viewer opens their project list.
The portal resolves the active grant against Registry.
outcomes: `not_found` counts as context that cannot be obtained, so P is omitted and the rest of the list is returned.
Only temporary dependency failures trigger omission; the definitive identity failure instead fails the list or follows another treatment not stated here.
witness.observer: The viewer reading the project list.
